sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: Consider a 10-class diagnostic classifier. Instance A outputs probabilities 0.491 and 0.490 in a tight two-class deadlock, while Instance B outputs diffuse noise spread between 0.12 and 0.16. Which metric prioritizes which candidate?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, let's see if our engineers can spot how Margin Sampling differs from Shannon Entropy across Instance A and Instance B!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on, Data Architect! Margin Sampling focuses purely on the top-two gap, scoring 0.001 on Instance A to break the binary diagnosis deadlock. Shannon Entropy evaluates total simplex dispersion, scoring near 2.95 bits on diffuse Instance B.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Least Confidence only checks the single maximum probability, missing second-place confusion entirely. Margin Sampling isolates binary boundary impasses like Instance A, whereas Shannon Entropy detects flat uniform uncertainty across all classes like Instance B.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In the Snorkel Weak Supervision Workbench, inspect Records 1 through 5 voted upon by 4 noisy rules. Naive majority voting ties on Record 2 and fails when noisy LF3 disagrees, scoring just 60 percent. Adjusting calibrated accuracy weights lets Snorkel's posterior recover 100 percent accuracy instantly.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at Record 2 and Record 3, Dr. Nova! Majority Vote got fooled down to 60 percent, while Snorkel's log-odds posterior hits 100 percent accuracy automatically!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: Two identical duplicate regex rules falsely output minus 1, while one independent 95-percent expert rule votes plus 1. Why does majority voting fail, and how does Snorkel resolve correlated LFs?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Two identical copied heuristics voting minus one against a 95-percent expert! Select the factor graph solution above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely right! Naive majority voting double-counts duplicated heuristics, defeating accurate rules 2 to 1. Snorkel's exponential factor graph detects high conditional covariance and adjusts pairwise dependency parameters theta_jk, shrinking duplicated mutual information back to one single vote.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Majority voting cannot detect redundant copies or enforce independence guarantees. Snorkel resolves correlated heuristics explicitly in the generative factor graph via pairwise dependency factors theta_jk calibrated on conditional covariances.
